{{Short description|Australian physicist (1922–2015)}}
{{Use Australian English|date=June 2020}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=January 2020}}
'''Harry Messel''', {{post-nominals|country=AUS|sep=,|AC|CBE}}, (3 March 1922 – 8 July 2015) was a Canadian-born [[Australia]]n [[physicist]] and [[education|educator]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.sbs.com.au/news/article/2015/07/08/scientist-harry-messel-dies-aged-93|title= Scientist Harry Messel dies aged 93|date=8 July 2015|publisher=[[SBS (Australian TV channel)|SBS TV]]|accessdate=9 July 2015}}</ref>

==Life and work==
Messel was born in [[Canada]] to [[Ukraine|Ukrainian]] parents.<ref name=ABCCat>{{cite news|url=http://www.abc.net.au/catalyst/stories/s1913589.htm|publisher=[[Australian Broadcasting Corporation]]|work=Catalyst|title=Professor Harry Messel}}</ref><ref name=BS>[http://www.asap.unimelb.edu.au/bsparcs/biogs/P000637b.htm Bright Sparcs entry on Harry Messel]</ref> He was born in [[Levine, Manitoba|Levine Siding]] in [[Manitoba]], and brought up in [[Rivers, Manitoba]]. He was accepted into the [[Royal Military College of Canada]].   During the [[World War II|Second World War]] he served as a [[paratrooper]] with the [[Canadian Forces]].<ref name=SoP/> He entered [[Queen's University at Kingston|Queen's University]] in Kingston, Ontario, in 1946, enrolling in both Honours Engineering Physics and an Honours Degree in Mathematics.

After fellowships at [[University of St Andrews]] and [[Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies]], Messel moved to Australia in 1951.<ref name=ABCCat/> He lectured in mathematical physics at the [[University of Adelaide]] 1951–52,<ref name=BS/> before being appointed in 1952 as Professor of Physics and Head of the School of Physics at the [[University of Sydney]], a position he held for 35 years until his retirement in 1987.  In 1952 he established the Nuclear Research Foundation, later known as the Science Foundation for Physics.<ref name=SoP>{{cite web|url=http://www.physics.usyd.edu.au/about/history.shtml|publisher=[[The University of Sydney]]|title=History of the School of Physics|work=School of Physics}}</ref><ref name=ME>{{cite web|url=http://www.physics.usyd.edu.au/messel/messel_professor.htm|title=Messel Endowment: Professor Harry Messel|work=School of Physics|publisher=[[The University of Sydney]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080722024114/http://www.physics.usyd.edu.au/messel/messel_professor.htm|archive-date=22 July 2008|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Messel was also [[Chancellor (education)#Australia|Chancellor]] and CEO of [[Bond University]] 1992–1997.<ref name="ME"/>

When the Soviet satellite, Sputnik 2, passed over the Southern Polar region in 1958, Messel recorded the encrypted data while the satellite was at its apogee of 1671&nbsp;km. However, the Soviets, who were unable to collect the data themselves, refused to release the interpreting code. When they asked Messel for the data, he told them to "go to hell".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://science.thewire.in/the-sciences/apollo-11-van-allen-radiation-belts-translunar-injection/#:~:text=What%20surrounds%20Earth%3F,a%20lethal%20dose%20of%20radiation.|title = How NASA Worked Around Earth's Radiation Belts to Land Apollo 11 on the Moon|date = 9 June 2019}}</ref>

In 1958 Professor Messel started the [[Professor Harry Messel International Science School|International Science School]] (ISS),<ref name=ISS>{{cite web|title=History of the International Science School|url=http://sydney.edu.au/science/physics/foundation/iss/history.shtml|website=University of Sydney Physics Foundation|publisher=University of Sydney|accessdate=11 July 2015}}</ref> which aims to encourage scientifically capable and interested students in their final two years of school to extend their knowledge and apply it to achieve progress. He frequently stated his discontent when sportsmen were praised and hailed whereas the next generation of scientists to change and run the world were given little to no encouragement. Since its inception, over 4,000 scholars have attended the ISS. The program runs once every two years with close to 150 students from up to 10 countries staying at [[The Women's College, University of Sydney|the Women's College]] for two weeks, attending lectures and participating in activities around the University of Sydney.

===Honours===
Messel was appointed a Commander of the [[Order of the British Empire]] (CBE) in the 1979 New Year's Honours list;<ref>{{cite web|url=https://honours.pmc.gov.au/honours/awards/1065006|title=MESSEL Harry: CBE|work=It's an Honour|publisher=[[Australian Government]]|date=1 January 1979|accessdate=6 January 2014}}</ref> and a Companion of the [[Order of Australia]] (AC) in the 2006 Australia Day Honours 2006 for his service to Australian science and to education as an outstanding educator raising awareness of the importance of the study of science and in particular physics, for instrumental contributions to improving science teaching in schools, and for conservation advocacy relating to endangered crocodile and alligator species.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://honours.pmc.gov.au/honours/awards/1131289|title=MESSEL Harry: AC|work=It's an Honour|publisher=[[Australian Government]]|date=26 January 2006|accessdate=6 January 2014}}</ref>

In 2014, Messel, along with [[Simon McKeon]], was awarded the [[Australian Academy of Science]]'s ''Academy Medal'', which recognises scientific contributions other than research. The award to Messel was made "in recognition of his conspicuous and enduring service to the cause of science in Australia".<ref>{{cite web|url = https://www.science.org.au/awardees-2014|title = Awardees for 2014 - Australian Academy of Science|publisher = Australian Academy of Science|access-date = 2015-07-08|url-status = dead|archiveurl = https://web.archive.org/web/20150709224424/https://www.science.org.au/awardees-2014|archivedate = 9 July 2015|df = dmy-all}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.abc.net.au/radionational/programs/scienceshow/top-honour-for-harry-messel/5490486|title = Top honour for Harry Messel|date = 30 May 2014|publisher = Australian Broadcasting Corporation|access-date=2015-07-09}}</ref>

===Personal life===
Messel was married to Patrica Pegram, a nurse from [[Sussex, England]] whom he met in Dublin. They had three daughters, Naomi, Wendy and Iona.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article23426345 | title=Wives of leading men: MRS. HARRY MESSEL She knows her atom bombs | newspaper=Argus | date=May 1954 }}</ref>
